sentences.zh: 而且我认为这其中有两个核心原因。

sentences.en: Reason number one is Edward VI, like Henry VIII, doesn't think a woman can be queen.
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是爱德华六世和亨利八世一样，认为女性不能成为女王。

sentences.en: He just thinks, bad idea, end of the Tudors.
sentences.zh: 他只是觉得，这主意太糟了，都铎王朝就此完结。

sentences.en: Because she'll be dominated by some husband.
sentences.zh: 因为她会被某个丈夫支配。

sentences.en: No one will listen to her.
sentences.zh: 没人会听她的。

sentences.en: Doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这说不通。

sentences.en: So, you know, best not to.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，最好还是别这样。

sentences.en: But, of course, then that raises the question, why does he later go on to Jane?
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，这就引出了一个问题，他后来为什么又选中了简？

sentences.en: And the answer, I think, where he skips it.
sentences.zh: 而我认为答案就在于他为什么要跳过她。

sentences.en: But hold on.
sentences.zh: 但等等。

sentences.en: But hold on.
sentences.zh: 但等等。

sentences.en: But also, just on Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，就伊丽莎白而言。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Isn't it also the fact she's illegitimate?
sentences.zh: 难道不是因为她是个私生女吗？

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: This is absolutely it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 完全就是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: He thinks, and he's not wrong, because everybody thinks it, that Mary and Elizabeth are both illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 他认为——而且他没想错，因为所有人都这么认为——玛丽和伊丽莎白都是私生女。

sentences.en: Now, that will seem weird to us, because we don't think they're illegitimate, because, of course, they were both queens of England.
sentences.zh: 这在我们看来可能会觉得很奇怪，因为我们不认为她们是私生女，毕竟，她们两人后来都成了英格兰女王。

sentences.en: But Henry VIII had explicitly said, and it goes back to Henry VIII's third succession act.
sentences.zh: 但亨利八世曾经明确说过，这要追溯到亨利八世的第三次王位继承法案。

sentences.en: So Henry VIII's legislation had explicitly said they are both illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利八世的立法曾明确指出她们两个都是私生女。

sentences.en: And Mary, because her mother, Catherine of Aragon, was married to him illegally, because she'd been married to his brother, Arthur, before that.
sentences.zh: 玛丽是因为她的母亲阿拉贡的凯瑟琳与他非法结婚，因为凯瑟琳在此之前曾嫁给过他的哥哥亚瑟。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth, because Anne Boleyn was a witch, married him through necromancy.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白是因为安妮·博林是个女巫，通过巫术嫁给了他。

sentences.en: And therefore, Elizabeth was also.
sentences.zh: 因此，伊丽莎白也是如此。

sentences.en: And there's no reason to believe that Edward VI, Edward VI completely believes this.
sentences.zh: 而且没有理由认为爱德华六世不信这个，爱德华六世对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: He thinks this is, he's thought this all his life.
sentences.zh: 他打小就这么认为，他一辈子都这么想。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, has Henry VIII also not made it a matter of statute that if Edward dies, then Mary and Elizabeth in turn will succeed?
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，亨利八世难道没有通过成文法规定，如果爱德华去世，接下来就轮到玛丽和伊丽莎白依次继位吗？

sentences.en: Well, this is the crazy ambiguity that in his third succession act and in his will, Henry VIII had basically laid down.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是那套疯狂的模棱两可之处，亨利八世在他的第三次继承法案和遗嘱中基本上就是这么规定的。

sentences.en: Yes, they're illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 是的，她们是私生女。

sentences.en: But in the line of succession, it's Edward first and then Mary and Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 但在继承顺位上，先是爱德华，然后是玛丽和伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: So it's very ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常含糊不清。

sentences.en: And actually, a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，很多人……

sentences.en: Well, you say it's ambiguous, but.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你说含糊不清，但是……

sentences.en: Because if they're illegitimate, how can they succeed?
sentences.zh: 因为如果她们是私生女，怎么能继位呢？

sentences.en: But it would never have been an issue had Edward not tried to make it an issue.
sentences.zh: 但如果爱德华不试图把这变成一个问题，这就根本不会是个问题。

sentences.en: Probably right.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: You're probably right.
sentences.zh: 你可能说得对。

sentences.en: He's only kind of using it as an excuse, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他其实只是把它当作一个借口，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, because actually, in the event, Mary proves to be the people's choice as queen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为事实上到头来，玛丽证明了自己才是人们心目中的女王人选。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth succeeds without any kind of people, with anyone complaining that she's illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白继位时，也没有任何人抱怨她是个私生女。

sentences.en: I don't think he's using it purely as an excuse to avoid a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他纯粹是借此作为排斥天主教徒的借口。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, why does he skip Elizabeth?
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，他为什么要跳过伊丽莎白？

sentences.en: Yeah, the king, wanting a male, I think, is also.
sentences.zh: 对，国王渴望有个男性继承人，我认为这也是……

sentences.en: I think wanting a male is crucial.
sentences.zh: 我认为渴望男性继承人至关重要。

sentences.en: So here's a key thing to remember, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一件需要记住的关键事情，汤姆。

sentences.en: At this point, he doesn't think he's going to die.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，他并不觉得自己会死。

sentences.en: And lots of people don't think he's going to die.
sentences.zh: 而且很多人也不觉得他会死。

sentences.en: He's just ill.
sentences.zh: 他只是生病了。

sentences.en: And in the way that, you know, when you really think about your will, that's what he's thinking about.
sentences.zh: 就像你在真正考虑自己的遗嘱时那样，这正是他当时的所思所想。

sentences.en: So in this first version, he says, listen, if I die without an heir, because obviously he thinks one day he'll get married and have kids.
sentences.zh: 所以在第一个版本中，他说，听着，如果我死时没有子嗣——因为他显然认为自己总有一天会结婚生子——

sentences.en: He says, if I die without an heir, it'll go to Lady Jane Grey's male heirs.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果我死时没有子嗣，王位将传给简·格雷女士的男性后嗣。

sentences.en: And if not her, then her sister's male, then her sister's sons.
sentences.zh: 如果没有她，就传给她姐姐的男性后嗣，然后是她姐姐的儿子们。

sentences.en: And if not her, then her sister's sons.
sentences.zh: 如果没有她，就传给她姐姐的儿子们。

sentences.en: So this is a sort of contingency plan.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种备用方案。

sentences.en: But then that all changes.
sentences.zh: 但随后这一切都变了。

sentences.en: Because on Sunday, the 28th of May, which is this crucial day, so we're still in 1553, the doctors, his doctors meet.
sentences.zh: 因为在5月28日星期日，这是至关重要的一天，当时还是1553年，医生们，也就是他的主治医生们开会了。

sentences.en: And they basically have a conference.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上开了一个闭门会商。

sentences.en: And they say, he's not getting better.
sentences.zh: 他们说，他的病情没有好转。

sentences.en: Do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: He's actually going to die.
sentences.zh: 他实际上快要死了。

sentences.en: And clearly that is communicated to him, because in the next two weeks, he goes back over this thing, his device for the succession, and he makes a crucial change.
sentences.zh: 显然这已经传达给了他，因为在接下来的两周里，他重新审视了这份关于王位继承的设想，并做出了一个至关重要的改变。

sentences.en: So instead of the crown going to Lady Jane's male heirs or her sister's male heirs, he adds the word and.
sentences.zh: 因此，王位不再传给简女士的男性后嗣或她姐姐的男性后嗣，他加了一个词“and”（和）。

sentences.en: So now it says Lady Jane and her heirs male.
sentences.zh: 所以现在上面写的是简女士和她的男性后嗣。

sentences.en: So in other words, if he drops dead tomorrow, this girl, Lady Jane Grey, will be the next ruler of England.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果他明天突然暴毙，这个女孩，简·格雷女士，将成为英格兰的下一位统治者。

sentences.en: And that's the crucial change.
sentences.zh: 这就是至关重要的改变。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I've got an obvious question.
sentences.zh: 那我有一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: A question that is asked by the splendidly named Richard Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 这个问题是由名字非常响亮的理查德·克伦威尔提出的。

sentences.en: I'm a big fan of Richard Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 我是理查德·克伦威尔的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Francis Grey, who is Lady Jane's mother and the daughter of Mary, who is the sister of Henry VIII, must have had a better claim than her daughter.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·格雷，她是简的母亲，也是玛丽的女儿，而玛丽又是亨利八世的姐姐，她的王位继承权一定比她的女儿更好。

sentences.en: If you're excluding Bloody Mary and Mary, Queen of Scots as Catholics, did anyone think of making Francis queen?
sentences.zh: 如果你把血腥玛丽和苏格兰女王玛丽作为天主教徒排除在外，有没有人想过让弗朗西斯当女王？

sentences.en: They didn't.
sentences.zh: 他们没有。

sentences.en: Because she was past childbearing age by that point.
sentences.zh: 因为当时她已经过了生育年龄。

sentences.en: So she wasn't going to have any male heirs.
sentences.zh: 所以她不可能再生育任何男性后嗣了。

sentences.en: Is that the reason?
sentences.zh: 这就是原因吗？

sentences.en: No, there's still a possibility that she could have a male heir.
sentences.zh: 不，她仍然有可能生下男性继承人。

sentences.en: So why is she excluded?
sentences.zh: 那她为什么被排除在外呢？

sentences.en: Why don't they exclude her?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不把她算进去？

sentences.en: Why do they exclude her?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要排除她？

sentences.en: That's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: And other people have asked that.
sentences.zh: 其他人也问过这个问题。

sentences.en: And the reason is some people think it's because she's thought of as unreliable.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，有些人认为这是因为她被认为靠不住。

sentences.en: She's thought of as kind of flighty and difficult.
sentences.zh: 她被认为有点轻浮、难以相处。

sentences.en: But also, not only is Francis seen as a bit flighty and flaky and difficult, but her husband, who is, what's his name?
sentences.zh: 而且，不仅弗朗西斯被认为有点轻浮、不靠谱和难以相处，还有她的丈夫，他叫什么名字来着？

sentences.en: He's called Henry, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他叫亨利，对吧？

sentences.en: He's Henry Grey, Marquess of Dorset.
sentences.zh: 他是多塞特侯爵亨利·格雷。

sentences.en: He's descended from Elizabeth Woodville.
sentences.zh: 他是伊丽莎白·伍德ville的后代。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is.
sentences.zh: 对，他是。

sentences.en: So all those Greys that were involved in Richard III and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以所有那些卷入理查德三世事件以及种种纷争的格雷家族成员……

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But clearly, Edward VI doesn't think much of him either.
sentences.zh: 但显然，爱德华六世也挺瞧不上他的。

sentences.en: So let's just skip them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还是把他们跳过吧。

sentences.en: So Edward VI is really fiddling with the succession here.
sentences.zh: 因此，爱德华六世在这里确实对王位继承进行了篡改。

sentences.en: And so people sometimes say, well, this is completely illegal.
sentences.zh: 所以人们有时会说，这完全是非法的。

sentences.en: A king can't just pick and choose.
sentences.zh: 国王不能随心所欲地挑选继承人。

sentences.en: But of course, there was a precedent for that because Henry VIII had been doing that.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这有先例可循，因为亨利八世一直在这么做。

sentences.en: So in a way, again, you can understand why Edward thinks that because he's seen his father fiddle again and again with the succession, succession acts and wills.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，你也能理解为什么爱德华会这么想，因为他看到自己的父亲一次又一次地篡改继承权、继承法案和遗嘱。

sentences.en: But it's the acts, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那是法案，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's the parliamentary acts.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是议会法案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Henry VIII had it agreed by Parliament.
sentences.zh: 亨利八世是通过议会批准的。

sentences.en: In legislation, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是通过立法，对。

sentences.en: In legislation.
sentences.zh: 是通过立法。

sentences.en: So that's the difference, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这才是区别所在，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, Edward doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，爱德华没有这么做。

sentences.en: What Edward does is he basically gets everybody to sign a document saying, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 爱德华的做法基本上是让每个人都在一份文件上签字，说，好吧，行。

sentences.en: So with the Privy Council, lots of judges, lots of peers.
sentences.zh: 所以包括枢密院、许多法官、许多贵族。

sentences.en: So they all sign up to this, but it's been done in a great rush because it hasn't really been communicated to the great mass of the public.
sentences.zh: 因此他们都签署了这份文件，但这是在极其仓促的情况下完成的，因为并没有真正向广大公众传达。

sentences.en: And does it have legal force, though, if it hasn't been approved by Parliament?
sentences.zh: 然而，如果没有经过议会批准，它具有法律效力吗？

sentences.en: Does changing previous act that's been decreed by a king and pass through Parliament, can he just do that?
sentences.zh: 改变之前由国王颁布并经议会通过的法案，他能直接这么做吗？

sentences.en: Well, lawyers argue about this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，律师们对此争论不休。

sentences.en: He gets lots of lawyers to tell him that it does.
sentences.zh: 他找了很多律师告诉他这样做是合法的。

sentences.en: But of course they tell him that because that's what he wants to do.
sentences.zh: 但他们当然会这么告诉他，因为这正是他想做的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But here's the thing, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但关键是，汤姆。

sentences.en: If they had told him that, he had died, Lady Jane Grey had become queen and then been unchallenged or had beaten off Mary,
sentences.zh: 如果他们告诉他可以，他死了，简·格雷女士成了女王并且随后没有遇到挑战或者击败了玛丽，

sentences.en: we wouldn't be doing this podcast and arguing about the legality of the…
sentences.zh: 我们就不会在这里录播客并争论……的合法性了

sentences.en: Yeah, but she didn't, did she?
sentences.zh: 对，但她没有成功，不是吗？

sentences.en: And a huge part of the reason why she didn't do it is because it was widely felt to be illegal.
sentences.zh: 她之所以没成功，很大一部分原因是因为人们普遍认为这是非法的。

sentences.en: A bit odd.
sentences.zh: 有点离谱。

sentences.en: I don't think it's any more odd.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得这有多离谱。

sentences.en: I don't think it's any more illegal necessarily than some of Henry VIII's fiddling, you know, declaring…
sentences.zh: 我不认为这比亨利八世的一些篡改行为——比如宣布……——更具非法性。

sentences.en: Yes, for example, one of the things that Henry VIII does is Henry VIII skips a whole branch completely, you know, randomly, which is the Scottish branch.
sentences.zh: 是的，举个例子，亨利八世做的事情之一就是完全凭空跳过了一个整个分支，你知道的，也就是苏格兰分支。

sentences.en: So he just leaps over that as though it doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他直接把那一支跳过去了，就好像它不存在一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 对，他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: But he has had it approved by Parliament.
sentences.zh: 但他让议会批准了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Fair enough, Tom.
sentences.zh: 也有道理，汤姆。

sentences.en: Tom, you know, we've been talking for half an hour and I never thought we would spend half an hour talking about genealogy and the constitution.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你知道的，我们已经聊了半个小时了，我从没想过我们会花半个小时来聊家谱和宪政。

sentences.en: Statutes and things.
sentences.zh: 成文法之类的事情。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I think we should take a break at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们现在应该休息一下。

sentences.en: When we come back, obviously we should talk about Jane herself.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，显然我们应该聊聊简本人。

sentences.en: We should.
sentences.zh: 我们确实应该。

sentences.en: We've barely mentioned, but there's also another key figure that we've barely mentioned, and that is John Dudley, the Duke of Northumberland, who is Jane's, not coincidentally,
sentences.zh: 我们几乎没怎么提过，但还有一个关键人物我们也几乎没提过，那就是诺森伯兰公爵约翰·达德利，他恰好是简的——这并非巧合——

sentences.en: Jane's father-in-law and has been, he's the kind of the greatest man in the realm.
sentences.zh: 简的公公，而且一直是王国中最有权势的人。

sentences.en: He is indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: He's a controversial figure, Tom, who we have fun with.
sentences.zh: 他是一个备受争议的人物，汤姆，我们聊起他很有意思。

sentences.en: So we'll come back and we will look at John Dudley and we will look at Lady Jane Grey.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会回来看看约翰·达德利，也会看看简·格雷女士。

sentences.en: So don't go away.
sentences.zh: 所以请不要走开。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《历史的沉淀》。

sentences.en: We are looking at Lady Jane Grey, the so-called Nine Days Queen.
sentences.zh: 我们正在关注简·格雷女士，也就是所谓的“九日女王”。

sentences.en: And as I said before the break, we've hardly mentioned her.
sentences.zh: 正如我在中场休息前所说，我们几乎没怎么提到她。

sentences.en: We will, I promise.
sentences.zh: 我们会的，我保证。

sentences.en: But before we come to her, let's come, Dominic, to John Dudley.
sentences.zh: 但在我们讲到她之前，多米尼克，让我们先来谈谈约翰·达德利。

sentences.en: Do you think he spoke with a Dudley accent?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他说话带有达德利口音吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Is that your assumption?
sentences.zh: 这是你的猜测吗？

sentences.en: I don't believe that you did.
sentences.zh: 我不相信你做过这事。

sentences.en: So the Dudleys.
sentences.zh: 所以说到达德利家族。

sentences.en: The Dudleys are one of the great families.
sentences.zh: 达德利家族是伟大的家族之一。

sentences.en: In Tudor history.
sentences.zh: 在都铎历史中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And in fact, I commend a new book by Joanne Paul, just out, which I was dipping into before this, The House of Dudley, A New History of Tudor England.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我推荐一本乔安妮·保罗刚出版的新书，我刚才还在翻阅，书名是《达德利家族：都铎英格兰新史》。

sentences.en: And John Dudley's father, Edmund, had basically been an accountant, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 约翰·达德利 的父亲埃德蒙基本上是个会计，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He got executed by Henry VIII for having been left over from the previous realm.
sentences.zh: 他被亨利八世处决了，因为他是前朝留下来的人。

sentences.en: It's really important.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要。

sentences.en: So John Dudley has the image of his father, you know, being executed.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰·达德利脑海里有他父亲被处决的影像，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that tells you something about the paranoia at the center of the Tudor court.
sentences.zh: 这说明了都铎宫廷核心地带存在的偏执心态。

sentences.en: Is it paranoia?
sentences.zh: 这是偏执吗？

sentences.en: I'm not, you know, paranoia, you've got to, it's kind of illogical, but I mean, it's kind of genuinely, it's entirely authentic.
sentences.zh: 我不是说，你知道的，偏执这东西，你得承认，它有点不合逻辑，但我的意思是，它确实是发自内心的，完全真实的。

sentences.en: Completely reasonable.
sentences.zh: 完全合乎情理。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's been disinherited, then he gets, you know, his father's inheritance back.
sentences.zh: 所以他被剥夺了继承权，后来，你知道的，他又拿回了他父亲的遗产。

sentences.en: He's not really the accountant type, is he?
sentences.zh: 他可真不是那种会计类型的人，对吧？

sentences.en: He's much more, he's a kind of Charles Brandon figure.
sentences.zh: 他更像，他有点像查尔斯·布兰登那类人物。

sentences.en: He's a kind of man.
sentences.zh: 他就是那种人。

sentences.en: In fact, he gets knighted by Charles Brandon, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 事实上，他被查尔斯·布兰登册封为骑士了，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's less of a kind of roister-doyster than Charles Brandon.
sentences.zh: 比起查尔斯·布兰登，他没那么喧闹浮夸。

sentences.en: So he's more, he's a military man.
sentences.zh: 所以他更偏向于，他是个军人。

sentences.en: He's a soldier.
sentences.zh: 他是个士兵。

sentences.en: He's very efficient.
sentences.zh: 他非常高效。

sentences.en: So John Dudley, so Northumberland, as he's always called in the, so he has a succession of titles.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰·达德利，也就是诺森伯兰，人们在书中总是这么叫他，他拥有过一连串的头衔。

sentences.en: He has first Warwick and then Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 他先是沃里克伯爵，然后是诺森伯兰公爵。

sentences.en: And Northumberland, he's a duke, which is also the kind of, so there are only kind of three dukes at that point.
sentences.zh: 而诺森伯兰，他是一位公爵，这也是那种，当时那种情况总共只有大约三个公爵。

sentences.en: There are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So to be duke of Northumberland is a very big deal.
sentences.zh: 所以能成为诺森伯兰公爵是一件了不起的大事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So whenever people tell this story, he is always the villain.
sentences.zh: 所以每当人们讲述这段历史时，他总是扮演大反派。

sentences.en: I mean, he's the villain of Edward VI Reign.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是爱德华六世统治时期的反派。

sentences.en: He's the villain of the Lady Jane Grey saga.
sentences.zh: 他是简·格雷女士传奇中的反派。

sentences.en: And I think most historians would say now that is completely unfair and wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数历史学家现在都会认为这完全不公平，也是错误的。

sentences.en: So he's always seen as this, because he's the sort of chief minister, as it were, he's seen as this Svengali controlling Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是被视作这样一个人，因为他算是首席大臣，他被视为控制爱德华六世的幕后操纵者。

sentences.en: But I think that's very unfair.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这非常不公平。

sentences.en: He's a military man, as you say.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他是个军人。

sentences.en: He fought the Scots.
sentences.zh: 他与苏格兰人作战。

sentences.en: He fought all the traditional enemies, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他与所有传统敌人作战。

sentences.en: He fought peasants.
sentences.zh: 他跟农民打过仗。

sentences.en: He's putting down rebellions and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他负责平定叛乱之类的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, he put down the, what's Ket's Rebellion?
sentences.zh: 是的，他平定了，凯特起义是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Ket's Rebellion, Rebellion Against Enclosures, which is actually very important in the context of this story.
sentences.zh: 凯特起义，反对圈地运动的起义，这在这个故事的背景下其实非常重要。

sentences.en: So he's seen, people think of him as very efficient, very farsighted.
sentences.zh: 因此人们认为他非常高效、非常有远见。

sentences.en: He had such a head, as somebody says, that he seldom went about anything, but he first conceived three or four purposes beforehand.
sentences.zh: 正如某人所说，他很有谋略，做任何事之前，往往都会先构思好三到四个目的。

sentences.en: So he's kind of, he's a planner.
sentences.zh: 所以他算是一个善于谋划的人。

sentences.en: You know, he's careful and cautious.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他小心谨慎。

sentences.en: And what happens is, at the beginning of Edward VI reign, Edward VI is sort of dominated, because obviously he's only nine, by Jane Seymour's brothers, Edward and Thomas.
sentences.zh: 情况是这样的，在爱德华六世统治初期，由于爱德华六世显然只有九岁，他主要受制于简·西摩的兄弟爱德华和托马斯。

sentences.en: First of all, they fall out with each other.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们俩闹翻了。

sentences.en: And then basically everybody falls out with Edward Seymour, the Duke of Somerset.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上所有人都和萨默塞特公爵爱德华·西摩闹翻了。

sentences.en: And Dudley becomes the sort of figurehead of the movement of all the other bigwigs against him.
sentences.zh: 而达德利成为了其他权贵联合反对他的运动中的某种精神领袖。

sentences.en: And Dudley then becomes the big man in Edward VI's council.
sentences.zh: 随后，达德利成了爱德华六世议会中的核心人物。

sentences.en: He's a big, he's a big Protestant, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他是个坚定的新教徒。

sentences.en: He's, he's very into his, his religious reform.
sentences.zh: 他非常热衷于他的宗教改革。

sentences.en: He's very serious about that.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常严肃认真。

sentences.en: He's big on law and order because he thinks the previous sort of administration made a mess of law and order.
sentences.zh: 他非常重视法律与秩序，因为他认为之前的政府把法治搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: He's also very big on financial retrenchment.
sentences.zh: 他也非常主张紧缩财政。

sentences.en: So, you know, he's, he's, he's sort of, I think he's, he's, most people would say he's actually a very good sort of governor, as it were, of, of England's affairs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他，他，他算是个，我想大多数人都会认为他实际上是管理英格兰事务的一个非常出色的管理者。

sentences.en: So he's kind of, the money is, is mounting up law and order.
sentences.zh: 所以资金在不断累积，法律和秩序也...

sentences.en: He's big on keeping sort of dissent to a minimum.
sentences.zh: 他非常主张将异见降到最低。

sentences.en: He's a, he, he doesn't really, I think it's fair to say, sort of dominate Edward VI as much as people used to think.
sentences.zh: 他，我觉得可以公正地说，他并没有像人们过去认为的那样完全主导爱德华六世。

sentences.en: Like, so Edward VI is probably much more of a partner with him.
sentences.zh: 就像，爱德华六世可能更像是他的合作伙伴。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously they're training Edward VI to be king, but basically Dudley is not just bossing Edward VI around, but Dudley is the big man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然他们在把爱德华六世培养成国王，但基本上达德利不仅仅是对爱德华六世颐指气使，达德利只是个大人物。

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot of people who don't like him.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有很多人不喜欢他。

sentences.en: There's lots of resentments.
sentences.zh: 有太多的怨恨。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And he has a lot of sons, one of whom, of course, will go on to become Elizabeth's favorite, Robert Dudley, the Earl of Leicester.
sentences.zh: 他有很多儿子，其中一个儿子后来自然成了伊丽莎白的宠臣——莱斯特伯爵罗伯特·达德利。

sentences.en: But for our purposes, the key one is, is a, he's called Guildford, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但对我们而言，关键的一个是，他叫吉尔福德，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this is the great what if, this is the great what if, Tom, in a different world, there's an England that had a King Guildford.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个巨大的假设，汤姆，这就是那个巨大的假设，在另一个世界里，英格兰曾有过一位吉尔福德国王。

sentences.en: King Guildford.
sentences.zh: 吉尔福德国王。

sentences.en: King Guildford the firSt.
sentences.zh: 吉尔福德一世。

sentences.en: And the people of Guildford would be delighted with that, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 吉尔福德的人民一定会为此高兴坏的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也不一定。

sentences.en: They'd be the royal borough of Guildford, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 他们会成为吉尔福德皇家自治市镇，对吧？

sentences.en: They would.
sentences.zh: 他们会的。

sentences.en: And I'm not knocking Guildford at all, but it's not the most automatically glamorous of places.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说吉尔福德不好，但它确实不是那种天然自带光环的地方。

sentences.en: And in many ways, the great tragedy of this story is that works out so badly for the people of Guildford who miss out on their chance.
sentences.zh: 从许多方面来看，这个故事最大的悲剧在于，吉尔福德的人民命运如此不济，他们错失了机会。

sentences.en: Who miss out on their chance at royal glory.
sentences.zh: 错失了他们获得皇家荣耀的机会。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So, so Guildford marries Lady Jane.
sentences.zh: 所以，吉尔福德娶了简女士。

sentences.en: Tremendous catch for him.
sentences.zh: 对他来说这是一桩了不起的婚事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the question then is, so it's usually assumed that Northumberland is doing the kind of equivalent of insider dealing, that he knows what's coming.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，通常人们认为诺森伯兰在搞类似于内幕交易的事情，他早就知道了内情。

sentences.en: He's had a look at Edward VI's device.
sentences.zh: 他看过爱德华六世的遗诏。

sentences.en: And so he's pairing his son up with the girl who may well become Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 所以他把他的儿子和那个很可能成为英格兰女王的女孩撮合在了一起。

sentences.en: But it's possible, isn't it, that actually it's the other way around?
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能，事实恰恰相反呢？

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But it's Edward VI who is pushing it.
sentences.zh: 其实是爱德华六世在极力推动此事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So what we don't know is if this whole scheme was cooked up by John Dudley or whether it was cooked up by Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道整个计划究竟是由约翰·达德利策划的，还是由爱德华六世策划的。

sentences.en: I think it seems, you know, there's a historian who's written an absolutely brilliant book on this called Eric Ives, who does treat it as a kind of whodunit and really digs into
sentences.zh: 我觉得似乎，有一位名叫埃里克·艾夫斯的历史学家写了一本绝对精彩的书来探讨此事，他把这当作一桩悬疑案来处理，并真正深入挖掘了

sentences.en: the motives of all the sort of the suspects and sort of the forensic analysis of the documents.
sentences.zh: 所有嫌疑人的动机，并对文件进行了司法鉴定级别的分析。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, it's actually not clear that the Guildford marriage is just because he knows
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，其实并不清楚吉尔福德的婚姻纯粹是因为他知道

sentences.en: Jane will be Queen.
sentences.zh: 简将会成为女王。

sentences.en: That actually the Guildford marriage to Jane may just be an absolutely standard, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上吉尔福德和简的联姻可能只是一桩绝对标准、你知道的

sentences.en: court marriage, and that actually at this point, Edward may not have changed his plans so that
sentences.zh: 宫廷婚姻，而且实际上在这个时候，爱德华可能还没有改变他的计划，好让

sentences.en: Jane herself will inherit.
sentences.zh: 简本人继承王位。

sentences.en: So if Northumberland had put his son up to this, you know, he'd be playing a hell of a long game because, I mean, it would be his grandchildren that would inherit the throne.
sentences.zh: 所以如果诺森伯兰是唆使他儿子这么做的，你知道的，那他就是在下一盘很大的棋，因为这意味着继承王位的是他的孙辈。

sentences.en: It's a long time in the future.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以后的事了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's still something to think about.
sentences.zh: 对，但那仍然是值得深思的一点。

sentences.en: It is still something.
sentences.zh: 这确实值得思考。

sentences.en: And of course, I'm sure there was a degree of self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，我确信其中存在一定程度的自私利益。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, there would be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是肯定的。

sentences.en: That's completely natural in a Tudor courtier.
sentences.zh: 这对于一个都铎王朝的朝臣来说是再自然不过的了。

sentences.en: But I think it's to see Dudley as the mastermind of the sort of conspirator plotting all this.
sentences.zh: 但我认为把达德利看作策划这一切的阴谋家、幕后主使

sentences.en: I think Rob's Edward VI of agency.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是剥夺了爱德华六世的主动性。

sentences.en: I think it's Edward VI's project, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我认为这是爱德华六世的计划。

sentences.en: So we have a question from Dr. Danny Witch-Hunting Buck.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个来自“猎巫”丹尼·巴克博士的问题。

sentences.en: Do you feel it was Edward's idealism or Dudley's ambition that put Lady Jane on the throne?
sentences.zh: 你觉得把简女士推上王位的是爱德华的理想主义，还是达德利的野心？

sentences.en: I suppose your answer to that, and I don't want to put words into your mouth, but I'm going to,
sentences.zh: 我想你对此的回答——我可不想把话塞进你嘴里，但我还是要说——

sentences.en: is that you would say that Dudley had a measure of idealism as well, that he's obviously ambitious,
sentences.zh: 你会说达德利也有一定程度的理想主义，他显然很有野心，

sentences.en: but presumably he shares Edward's anxiety about, well, definitely Mary, because Mary and Northumberland hate each other.
sentences.zh: 但想必他也认同爱德华对玛丽的担忧——绝对是针对玛丽，因为玛丽和诺森伯兰互不相容。

sentences.en: But there's also a kind of religious dimension to that.
sentences.zh: 但这其中也有一种宗教层面的维度。

sentences.en: Northumberland is a radical Protestant, doesn't want Catholics back.
sentences.zh: 诺森伯兰是个激进的新教徒，不希望天主教卷土重来。

sentences.en: He thinks it will guarantee a Protestant England.
sentences.zh: 他认为这能确保英格兰维持新教信仰。

sentences.en: It happens to suit him.
sentences.zh: 这恰好也对他的胃口。

sentences.en: You know, his son will be effectively king.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他的儿子实际上将成为国王。

sentences.en: So idealism and ambition kind of concur.
sentences.zh: 所以理想主义和野心在某种程度上是不谋而合的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I don't think he thinks, oh, I've masterminded this huge thing.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他觉得自己“噢，我策划了这么大一出戏”。

sentences.en: This is my splendid fiendish plot.
sentences.zh: “这是我精妙绝伦的邪恶计划。”

sentences.en: And it's pretty clear that he hasn't planned every detail in the way that he normally does.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，他并没有像往常那样把每一个细节都计划周全。

sentences.en: So you've got this meticulous, hard-nosed planner who is desperately improvising and making stuff up as he goes along.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是一个一丝不苟、冷酷无情的谋划者在走一步算一步，绝望地临场发挥。

sentences.en: And people think that at the time, don't they?
sentences.zh: 当时的人们也是这么认为的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because this is the age of Machiavelli and the image of the Machiavelli, a sinister kind of figure plotting and pulling strings behind the scenes, has become part of the kind of
sentences.zh: 因为这是马基雅维利的时代，马基雅维利的形象——那种在幕后密谋、操纵傀儡的阴险人物——已经成为了

sentences.en: the mental furniture of people in this period.
sentences.zh: 这个时期人们思维定式的一部分。

sentences.en: And so I guess that that must be part of why Northumberland comes to get such a dark reputation is that people associate him with Machiavellian devices and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，这也是诺森伯兰为什么会落得如此黑暗名声的部分原因，因为人们将他与马基雅维利式的阴谋诡计之类的事情联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 对，我认为完全是这样。

sentences.en: I think it also, when the whole thing unravels, everybody blames him.
sentences.zh: 我认为当整件事情败露时，所有人都把责任推到了他头上。

sentences.en: You know, all the other people who were in on it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所有其他参与其中的人都是如此。

sentences.en: Which is convenient, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很方便，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's a convenient scapegoat.
sentences.zh: 他是一个方便的替罪羊。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a slight tradition, isn't there, in Tudor, England, of basically the last king's chief minister gets the chop as soon as the successor comes in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在都铎时期的英格兰，基本上有一点传统，就是前任国王的首席大臣一旦新君即位就会人头落地。

sentences.en: So there's a sense in which, you know, that happened to his own father.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，你知道的，他的亲生父亲就遭遇过这种事。

sentences.en: His dad.
sentences.zh: 他爸爸。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he basically ends up, it's the same story again.
sentences.zh: 而他最后基本上也落得如此下场，历史重演了。

sentences.en: I mean, he basically carries the can for all the resentments that are piled up at the end of the reign of Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他基本上承担了爱德华六世统治末期积聚的所有怨气。

sentences.en: And I think there is that dimension in early modern history generally, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 我认为早期现代历史中普遍存在这种维度，不是吗？

sentences.en: The sort of Cardinal Richelieu, the éminence grise, the power behind the throne.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的黎塞留枢机主教、幕后权臣、王权背后的实力派。

sentences.en: And that's what historians talk about, the sort of black legend of Northumberland as this sort of plotter par excellence.
sentences.zh: 这就是历史学家所说的诺森伯兰的黑色传奇，把他描绘成那种完美的阴谋家。

sentences.en: But it's also with the idea of the Machiavelli that it's power for power's sake, that there's
sentences.zh: 但这其中也带有马基雅维利主义的思想，即为了权力而权力，

sentences.en: not a shred of idealism about it, that it's just about doing down your rivals and making yourself top dog.
sentences.zh: 里面没有一丝一毫的理想主义，纯粹是为了打压竞争对手并登上权力巅峰。

sentences.en: And clearly that's not all it is for Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 很显然，诺森伯兰的情况并非全然如此。

sentences.en: I mean, it must be a huge part of it, but that's not all it is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这肯定占了很大一部分，但并不全是这样。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So that's Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 这就是诺森伯兰的情况。

sentences.en: Now, what about the lady herself, Lady Jane Grey, who of course isn't Lady Jane Grey by this point, is she?
sentences.zh: 那么，这位女主角本身呢，简·格雷女士，当然她此时已经不叫简·格雷女士了，对吧？

sentences.en: She must be Lady Jane Dudley.
sentences.zh: 她一定成了达德利夫人。

sentences.en: Well, she's Jane Grey when she, yes, she becomes, I hadn't thought of that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当她……是的，她变成了，我之前没想到这一点。

sentences.en: She does become Jane Dudley, but at this point she's Jane Grey.
sentences.zh: 她确实变成了简·达德利，但在此时她还是简·格雷。

sentences.en: So what can we say about her?
sentences.zh: 我们能对她作何评价？

sentences.en: Well, as always, I think with Tudor England, as a sort of modern historian looking at this period, I think what's so interesting about it is that the sources are so tantalizing,
sentences.zh: 嗯，和往常一样，我觉得对于都铎时期的英格兰来说，作为一个研究这一时期的现代历史学家，我觉得最有趣的是这些历史资料极其引人入胜，

sentences.en: they give you just enough that you can construct a kind of personality out of these historical characters.
sentences.zh: 它们恰到好处地提供了一些线索，让你能够从这些历史人物身上拼凑出某种性格。

sentences.en: But actually, you know, the imagination is doing an enormous amount of the legwork.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道的，很大一部分工作其实是靠想象力完成的。

sentences.en: So we actually know quite, you know, it's frustrating how little we know about Jane, but actually what we know about her is all to her credit, by and large.
sentences.zh: 所以我们其实很清楚……你知道的，我们对简的了解少得令人沮丧，但实际上我们对她的了解大体上都对她很有利。

sentences.en: So she's born probably in 1537.
sentences.zh: 她大概出生于1537年。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't even know the year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们甚至连具体年份都不知道。

sentences.en: We can't even be absolutely certain of the year.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至无法百分之百确定年份。

sentences.en: She's probably born or brought up in this house, Bradgate Park near Leicester.
sentences.zh: 她可能出生或成长在这栋房子里，也就是莱斯特附近的布拉德盖特公园。

sentences.en: So it's the sort of one of the great brick mansions that belong to the Grey family.
sentences.zh: 所以这是格雷家族名下的那类宏伟砖砌宅邸之一。

sentences.en: Her parents are very young when she's born.
sentences.zh: 她出生时，她的父母非常年轻。

sentences.en: So they're probably 20 and 21, respectively.
sentences.zh: 他们当时可能分别只有20岁和21岁。

sentences.en: What we know about her is that she, we have one physical description that comes from a nine day queen in Broglio.
sentences.zh: 我们对她的了解是，我们有一份来自布罗利奥对“九日女王”的外貌描述。

sentences.en: And he said, she has small features and a well-made nose, the mouth flexible and the lips red.
sentences.zh: 他说，她五官小巧，鼻子长得很好，嘴唇灵活且呈红色。

sentences.en: The eyebrows are arched and darker than her hair, which is nearly red.
sentences.zh: 她的眉毛弯曲，颜色比几乎呈红色的头发要深。

sentences.en: Her eyes are sparkling and reddish brown in colour.
sentences.zh: 她的眼睛炯炯神，呈红褐色。

sentences.en: I stood so near her grace that I noticed her colour was good, but freckled.
sentences.zh: 我离她这位阁下很近，注意到她气色很好，但长了雀斑。

sentences.en: When she smiled, she showed her teeth, which are white and sharp in all, a gracious and animated figure.
sentences.zh: 当她微笑时，露出了洁白而整齐的牙齿，总的来说，这是一个优雅而生动的形象。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So on her, on, on the question of schooling, uh, the reputation is that she's a brilliant, mind, right?
sentences.zh: 那么关于她的教育问题，普遍传言她是个天才，对吧？

sentences.en: She kind of speaks nine languages and can construe Hebrew and all kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 她好像会说九种语言，还能翻译希伯来语以及各种乱七八糟的东西。

sentences.en: Is, is that accurate?
sentences.zh: 这……这准确吗？

sentences.en: Where is that coming from?
sentences.zh: 这种说法是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: So this comes from, it's, it's the classic Tudor history thing where there's the one source, the one fragment on which people have built up a whole edifice of speculation.
sentences.zh: 所以这源于……这是都铎历史研究中的经典现象，即仅凭单一的资料、单一的片段，人们就构建起了一整套猜测的宏伟大厦。

sentences.en: But basically there's a humanist scholar called Roger Asham, who in 1550, so how old is she then?
sentences.zh: 但基本上有一位名叫罗杰·阿沙姆的人文主义学者，在1550年时——那她当时多大？

sentences.en: She's about 13.
sentences.zh: 她大约13岁。

sentences.en: Um, he visits Braggate in Leicester, uh, to visit her tutor, who's another great humanist called John Aylmer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他拜访了莱斯特的布拉德盖特，去探访她的家庭教师，那是另一位名叫约翰·艾尔默的伟大的人文主义者。

sentences.en: Um, and of course this is a great age of humanist scholars.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然这是一个人文主义学者辈出的伟大时代。

sentences.en: And he, um, Asher says, because he wrote about it, he said, before I went to Germany, I came
sentences.zh: 他，嗯，阿沙姆说——因为他对此有文字记载——他说，在我去德国之前，我来到

sentences.en: to Braggate in Leicestershire to late take my leave of that noble lady, Jane Gray, to whom I was exceedingly much beholding.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特郡的布拉德盖特，向那位我极其感激的高贵女士简·格雷辞行。

sentences.en: And he says, everybody else in the household was out hunting in the park, but I found her in her chamber reading Fido Platonis in Greek, so reading Plato.
sentences.zh: 他说，家里的其他人都在公园里打猎，但我发现她在自己的房间里用希腊语读柏拉图的《斐多篇》，也就是在读柏拉图。

sentences.en: And that with as much delight as some gentlemen would read a merry tale in Boccaccio.
sentences.zh: 而且她读得津津有味，就像某些绅士读薄伽丘的滑稽故事一样专心。

sentences.en: And after salutation and duty done with some other talk, I asked her why she should lose, why she would lose such pastime in the park.
sentences.zh: 在行礼问候并寒暄了一番之后，我问她为什么要把时间浪费在……为什么要在公园里错过这样的消遣。

sentences.en: I, why isn't she off in the park with everybody else?
sentences.zh: 我问，她为什么不和其他人一起去公园呢？

sentences.en: Smiling, she answered me, I wist all their sport in the park is but a shadow to that pleasure that I find in Plato.
sentences.zh: 她微笑着回答我，我深知他们在公园里的所有乐趣，与我在柏拉图身上找到的乐趣相比，不过是一个影子罢了。

sentences.en: Alas, good folk, they never felt what true pleasure meant.
sentences.zh: 唉，可怜的人们，他们从未体会过什么是真正的乐趣。

sentences.en: And she, you know, she can't get enough Plato.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，她对柏拉图百读不厌。

sentences.en: Oh no!
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪！

sentences.en: Well, that redounds immensely to her credit, rather than going off and having fun.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比起出去玩乐，这为她赢得了极高的声誉。

sentences.en: But there is a catch.
sentences.zh: 但这里有个问题。

sentences.en: So he, he basically says, you know, what, what's all that about?
sentences.zh: 所以他，他基本上是说，你知道的，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: You're a teenager.
sentences.zh: 你只是个青少年。

sentences.en: You shouldn't be out like, you know, killing animals with the, with the rest of your family.
sentences.zh: 你不应该像……你知道的，和家里的其他人一样去猎杀动物。

sentences.en: And she says, um, well, I'll tell you a truth, which you, maybe you'll marvel at.
sentences.zh: 而她说，嗯，好吧，我来告诉你一个真相，你听了也许会感到惊叹。

sentences.en: Um, one of the greatest benefits that God ever gave me, says Jane, is that he sent me so sharp and severe parents and so gentle as schoolmaster.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简说，上帝赐予我的最大恩惠之一，就是送给我如此严厉苛刻的父母以及如此温和的家庭教师。

sentences.en: Cause she goes, she says, you know, my schoolmaster, your mate gives me all these books.
sentences.zh: 因为她说，你知道的，我的家庭教师，也就是你的朋友，给了我所有这些书。

sentences.en: And we talk about this lovely, but when I'm in the presence of my father and my mother, whether I speak you silent, sit, stand, or go eat, drink, be merry or sad, blah, blah,
sentences.zh: 我们谈论这一切是多么美好，但当我在我父亲和母亲面前时，无论我是说话还是沉默、是坐着、站着还是走动、是吃喝、是高兴还是难过，喋喋不休，

sentences.en: blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 喋喋不休，喋喋不休。

sentences.en: I must do it so perfectly, um, as God made the world, or else I'm so sharply taunted, so cruelly threatened with pinches, nips, and bobs that I think myself in hell.
sentences.zh: 我都必须做到完美无缺，就像上帝创造世界那样，否则我就会受到严厉的斥责，遭到掐、拧和拍打等残酷的威胁，让我觉得自己身处地狱。

sentences.en: So in other words, she basically is escaping from being pinched by her parents.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她基本上是在逃避被父母虐待的现实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, if she's not good at killing animals, then that's awful, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，如果她不擅长猎杀动物，那可就太糟了，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you can imagine her father kind of, no, not like that, like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，你可以想象她父亲那种态度：不，不是那样，要这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Shoot it.
sentences.zh: 开枪打它。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: So basically in Tudor historiographical style, people have spent, you know, entire careers arguing about.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上在都铎历史编纂学的风格中，人们已经花了……你知道的，整个职业生涯来争论这些。

sentences.en: Well, there's enough grift there for a novel, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里面的素材足够写一部小说了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Is she exaggerating?
sentences.zh: 她是不是在夸大其词？

sentences.en: Is she, is she a stroppy teenager just saying, oh, my parents treat me.
sentences.zh: 她是不是，她是不是一个叛逆的青少年，只是在抱怨，噢，我的父母这样对待我。

sentences.en: They don't understand me.
sentences.zh: 他们不理解我。

sentences.en: They pinch me, um, or is this the truth?
sentences.zh: 他们掐我，嗯，还是说这就是事实？

sentences.en: Uh, and, uh, and is she this trend of smile?
sentences.zh: 呃，而且，呃，她真的是这种充满微笑的性格吗？

sentences.en: I mean, she's, by the way, there was one other thing about her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，顺便说一句，关于她还有另一件事。

sentences.en: It's a man called Sir Thomas Chaloner.
sentences.zh: 有个叫托马斯·查洛纳爵士的人。

sentences.en: He said, this would have definitely appealed to you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他说，这肯定会吸引你，汤姆。

sentences.en: He said, um, she had joined Chaldean words to the language of the Arabs with a skillful grasp of the idiom of the Hebrews.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，她将迦勒底语融入阿拉伯语的语言中，并对希伯来语的习语有着精湛的掌握。

sentences.en: For to mention her speaking on Greek or Latin would be a small account.
sentences.zh: 因为要提她对希腊语或拉丁语的掌握，那就微不足道了。

sentences.en: Other women speak these languages in civilized places.
sentences.zh: 其他文明地方的女性也会说这些语言。

sentences.en: Likewise, Gaelic and Etruscan speech had added their number to this English lady.
sentences.zh: 同样，盖尔语和伊特鲁里亚语也为这位英格兰女士的语言库增添了数量。

sentences.en: If you were to number her languages, this one lady spoke eight.
sentences.zh: 如果你要数数她掌握的语言，这位女士足足会说八种。

sentences.en: So, Tom, do you speak Chaldean?
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，你会说迦勒底语吗？

sentences.en: Chaldean.
sentences.zh: 迦勒底语。

sentences.en: Chaldean.
sentences.zh: 迦勒底语。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: I think that's all very improbable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这一切都非常不可信。

sentences.en: Do you think she speaks Etruscan?
sentences.zh: 你觉得她会说伊特鲁里亚语吗？

sentences.en: No, because nobody speaks Etruscan.
sentences.zh: 不会，因为根本没人会说伊特鲁里亚语。

sentences.en: Unless by Etruscan, they mean Tuscan, i.e. Italian.
sentences.zh: 除非他们说的伊特鲁里亚语是指托斯卡纳语，也就是意大利语。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But if it's Etruscan, then that's clearly a lie because nobody speaks Etruscan because they still haven't deciphered it.
sentences.zh: 但如果真的是伊特鲁里亚语，那显然是个谎言，因为没有人会说伊特鲁里亚语，由于至今尚未破译它。

sentences.en: So there are some people who say, historians who say this is humanists, humanist scholars.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人说，有历史学家说这是人文主义者，人文主义学者的行为。

sentences.en: Kind of boasting.
sentences.zh: 有点像在吹牛。

sentences.en: Massively exaggerating.
sentences.zh: 极大地夸大其词。

sentences.en: They're also her father, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，其实也有她父亲的成分在里面。

sentences.en: I mean, you did an impersonation of him as a sort of huntsman, but actually her father is quite into this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你把她父亲模仿成某种猎人的形象，但实际上她的父亲对这些很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So he's a patron for the lot of them and a good contact.
sentences.zh: 所以他是所有这些人的赞助人，也是个很好的联系人。

sentences.en: So they probably want to butter him up by, like, bigging him up in their letters to each other.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们可能会在彼此的书信中通过拼命夸赞他来讨好他。

sentences.en: So there's an element of that about it as well.
sentences.zh: 所以其中也包含这方面的因素。

sentences.en: But Jane saying, oh, I hate them.
sentences.zh: 但简却说，哦，我讨厌他们。

sentences.en: They, you know, they're constantly criticizing me.
sentences.zh: 他们，你知道的，他们总是挑剔我。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That does sound kind of, I mean, you can imagine her father like kind of competitive dad in the far show.
sentences.zh: 听起来确实有点……我的意思是，你可以想象她父亲就像育儿秀里那种好胜的父亲。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I mean, I don't think there's any reason to doubt that it's the one thing we know.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我的意思是，我认为没有任何理由怀疑这就是我们所了解的唯一事实。

sentences.en: I mean, it's also, and I think that there's no reason to doubt she's a great reader.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这也是，而且我认为没有理由怀疑她是一个酷爱读书的人。

sentences.en: She loves speaking languages.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢说各种语言。

sentences.en: She likes talking to scholars.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢与学者交谈。

sentences.en: That is absolutely consistent.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对一致的。

sentences.en: And I mean, the reason we can be pretty sure it's consistent is that when we get to the end of her life, when she's in the tower, you know, she's writing letters, she's reading
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之所以能相当确定这是一致的，是因为当我们走到她生命的尽头，当她身处伦敦塔时，你知道的，她在写信，她在读

sentences.en: the Bible.
sentences.zh: 圣经。

sentences.en: She's being very, very serious and having theological arguments with people.
sentences.zh: 她变得非常非常严肃，并与人进行神学辩论。

sentences.en: Um, so she's absolutely, I mean, she is another red hot Protestant.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以她绝对是……我的意思是，她是另一个狂热的清教徒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's, that's the key thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这才是关键所在，对吧？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't really matter for the purposes of Edward VI or Northumberland, how clever she is, how many ancient languages she can read, any of that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于爱德华六世或诺森伯兰的目标来说，她有多聪明、她能阅读多少种古代语言，这些其实都不重要。

sentences.en: What matters is her bloodline and the fact that she is as committed and white hot a Protestant as they are.
sentences.zh: 重要的是她的血统，以及她和他们一样坚定、狂热地信仰新教这一事实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's all that matters.
sentences.zh: 而这才是唯一重要的。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: So to return to the sort of narrative, so Jane marries Guilford Dudley, um, their, their contract, their sort of, the arrangement is made.
sentences.zh: 因此，回到叙事上来，简嫁给了吉尔福德·达德利，嗯，他们的婚约，他们某种程度上的安排达成了。

sentences.en: Guilford gets food poisoning, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 吉尔福德食物中毒了，对吧？

sentences.en: At the, at the wedding.
sentences.zh: 在婚礼上。

sentences.en: Well, the Dudleys have terrible trouble with their health.
sentences.zh: 嗯，达德利家族的健康状况一直有很大的问题。

sentences.en: So, so John Dudley is a hypochondriac who apparently has this stomach ulcer or stomach issues that mean he's often missing.
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰·达德利是个疑病症患者，据说他有胃溃疡或肠胃问题，导致他经常缺席。

sentences.en: So yeah, as well as being this incredibly impressive military man, um, he's got this, he's a, he's a martyr to his stomach.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，除了是一个极其出色的军事家之外，嗯，他还饱受胃病的折磨。

sentences.en: Well, because they hardly ever spend any time together because, um, Guilford gets, gets food poisoning at the wedding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他们几乎没怎么在一起待过，因为，嗯，吉尔福德在婚礼上食物中毒了。

sentences.en: He's sick for a month and then he recovers and Jane immediately gets food poisoning.
sentences.zh: 他病了一个月，然后刚康复，简马上又食物中毒了。

sentences.en: So, so, so.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，所以。

sentences.en: Difficult for the happy couple.
sentences.zh: 这对新婚夫妇真是历经坎坷。

sentences.en: Jane's illness may be stressed by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，简的生病可能也是因为压力过大。

sentences.en: She may be, she may be conscious that some terrible, you know, um, crisis is looming and she may be, you know, she may have detected a change in the atmosphere, but also funny
